result.rationale: In the Google CalendarService, selectedCalendar is now computed as destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId, falling back to 'primary'. EventManager's legacy branch (destination.credentialId falsy) calls createEvent(c, event) for all matching credentials; for such destinations no calendar in the array matches the credentialId, so the find returns undefined and events go to 'primary' instead of the previously used calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.externalId. This is a verifiable behavioral regression introduced by this diff.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts around line 147, the code changed from using `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.externalId` directly to `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`. This means if a destination calendar exists but has no credentialId (legacy case), the find() will return undefined, and selectedCalendar will be undefined, falling back to 'primary'. In EventManager.ts, the legacy branch (lines 377-382) handles destinations without credentialId by filtering calendarCredentials by integration type and calling createEvent for each. However, when createEvent is called, it passes the credential but the GoogleCalendarService.createEvent now requires the credentialId to match in the destinationCalendar array. Since legacy destinations don't have credentialId set, the find() won't match, causing events to be created on 'primary' instead of the intended destination calendar.
